title: Varied band experience and advice to young musicians
summary: Armstrong lists Erskine Tate at the Vendome, Fletcher Henderson, Fate Marable's boat band, Joe Glaser at the Sunset and Carroll Dickerson, and advises youngsters to play with good musicians.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Well now as a trumpet player, did it give you more scope to play in a group like this?

Well, I didn't very much attention to the idea of, you know, what I was going to do. I went with so many different organizations. I went with Burst Ketate at the Vendome at that time. And as you go along, you know, you're changing styles. And I was playing for silent pictures, big old symphony orchestra playing for silent pictures. And after the curtain go up, you play on the chair and a hot number. That's where I came in, you know. And as the years go on, you lose a lot. It's impossible that you do that, you know.
But that was really the first thing that I lost the memory.

Well, that was my life. That's all I knew of. Sure. But you have to get with different. Now like when I went with Fletcher Anderson's band in 1924. Well, there was something else. There was Don Richmond. The minute I get up on the stand to join the band, there's a part in front of me. You know, well, I was at least tall. And you get conscious. You know, your mind, as you go along, you've got to get with it. Yeah. So you lose something. But is that all good experience for you as a musician? I enjoy the experience. But, I mean, what about the record collectors? A lot of them, they figure, well, I shouldn't have never done it. Oh. But to me, I thought, well, every time I look around I was playing with good musicians. And like I played on the excursion boats with Fate Marables band. That was a good band, 1919 to 1921. That's where I used to meet Bix up and down that Mississippi River there on that excursion boat from St. Louis to Davenport. Yeah. And I used to see a little youngster. Yeah. And then we'd start meeting all over the country. And sit down. We had sessions. And I enjoyed it all. And then I went into the Sunset with Joe Glazer in 1926. And I was doubling from the Sunset to the Vendome. So there was a lot of experience in this. Carol Dixon, big band, you know.

So all this added to your own equipment as a truck. As a truck. Yeah. And I didn't try to do nothing else but blows. And you would advise any youngster today to, I would assume, to have as much experience as a concert?

Experience, you should always play with good musicians if they can and try to listen to them and see what they put down. And that's the way I came along. You know. I didn't try to overdo it or not. I just enjoyed playing them good bands. That's all.
